title: Austin monthly mixed-beverage receipts, year over year
brief: Revision 2 applies the owner's decisions of 2026-11-08. The question is unchanged: entrants forecast Austin's mixed-beverage receipts for a coming month as 100 x the month's total over the same month last year. The data is the Texas Comptroller's file on Texas Open Data (naix-2893). It is keyless and updates every Saturday. Forecasts lock before the month starts. Rounds resolve on the snapshot from the last day of the following month. Decided: the ranked zero point is same-as-last-year with a 12-month RMS spread, written as the parameterised reference yoy(k=0, spread=rms12). October and November 2026 run as unscored pilot rounds. The rights verdict is proposed as 'permission-needed', and the question to the portal is drafted. For maintainers: confirm the rights verdict, and decide whether a person may read the terms page and send the drafted question. No scored round runs before written permission or the maintainers' clearance. The first scored lock is Sun 2027-01-31, if that clearance has arrived by then.
question: What will Austin's total reported mixed-beverage gross receipts (liquor, wine, beer and cover charges) for the target calendar month be, as an index of 100 x (target-month total / same month a year earlier), reading the target month from the resolution snapshot and the year-earlier month from the snapshot archived at lock?

source.publisher: Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts, published on the Texas Open Data Portal (data.texas.gov, run by the Texas Department of Information Resources on Tyler/Socrata). Dataset 'Mixed Beverage Gross Receipts', naix-2893, attribution 'Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts', provenance 'official' [verified 2026-11-09T00:58:57Z]. Portal publishing contact: txopendataportal@dir.texas.gov [unverified; from a search result for texas.gov].
source.access: Socrata SODA endpoint https://data.texas.gov/resource/naix-2893.json. No key, no app token and no account [verified: five unauthenticated grouped queries returned HTTP 200 on 2026-11-09 between 00:58Z and 01:01Z, 0.5 to 5.4 s each]. The doc suggests a free app token. That would mean signing up for an account, so the card does not use one. Fetch: once a day, at 14:00 UTC, one grouped request. Updates land on Saturdays at about 08:32 UTC, so a daily fetch also catches the off-cycle Wednesday loads seen in holiday weeks. Request: GET .../resource/naix-2893.json?$select=obligation_end_date_yyyymmdd as d, sum(total_receipts) as tot, sum(liquor_receipts) as liq, sum(wine_receipts) as wine, sum(beer_receipts) as beer, sum(cover_charge_receipts) as cover, count(*) as n&$where=upper(location_city)='AUSTIN' AND obligation_end_date_yyyymmdd >= '<fetch day - 800 days>'&$group=d&$order=d&$limit=5000. This is about 27 rows, under 5 KB. Write the body exactly as served to sources/tx_mixbev/<YYYY-MM-DD>.json, with url, fetched_at, sha256, bytes and changed_at in sources/manifest.json via ssa/provenance.py. The archive is the resolution source: the live endpoint cannot be read as of a past date. Rows are replaced, not versioned. Venue-period pairs are unique (0 duplicates for Sep 2025 [verified]), and rows for old months are deleted and re-inserted every week (see evidence), so only the archive shows what a past snapshot held. The refresh runs on datacenter runners, and that route has not been tested. A 403 or 429 on the first pilot day means a local courier is needed (lesson 3).
source.archive_policy: Use: allowed, inferred. Automated retrieval: allowed by intent, inferred. Redistribution of archived bodies: unclear. Evidence: (a) Dataset metadata has licenseId null and license null. It names the publisher and links only the Comptroller privacy policy [verified, api/views/naix-2893.json, 2026-11-09T00:58:57Z]. The doc found the same on 2026-11-06. (b) The portal footer's 'Terms of Service' link points to http://www.socrata.com/terms-of-service. That redirects to support.socrata.com/hc/en-us/articles/360019057154, which returned HTTP 403 [verified, 2026-11-09T01:06Z]. data.texas.gov/terms-of-service returned 404. So the platform terms are unread [unverified]. (c) The DIR portal page describes the portal as 'the official State of Texas repository for publicly accessible open data sets'. It states no reuse licence [verified via fetch, dir.texas.gov/office-chief-data-officer/texas-open-data-portal, 2026-11-09]. (d) Tex. Gov't Code §2054.1265 (SB 701, 2011) requires an agency's high-value data sets to be 'raw data in open standard format that allows the public to search, extract, organize, and analyze the information' [unverified: read from a bill analysis in search results, not the current statute text]. (e) The Comptroller's policies index has no copyright, reuse or automation clause [verified via fetch, comptroller.texas.gov/about/policies/, 2026-11-09]. Reading: (d) and the portal's purpose support use and API retrieval. Nothing found grants redistribution, and nothing forbids it. Lesson 1 says 'not forbidden' is not permission. Proposed inventory row (owner decision, rev 2): rights 'permission-needed'. This is proposed for maintainers, not granted. No scored round runs until there is written permission or the maintainers clear the verdict. The pilot may archive privately. Task for a person, once a maintainer says go (nobody sends anything before that): (1) In an ordinary browser, open https://support.socrata.com/hc/en-us/articles/360019057154, the portal footer's Terms of Service, which returned 403 here. Save the text and its date, and record any clause on automated access, archiving or redistribution in this card's evidence. (2) Send the following message. Message, to txopendataportal@dir.texas.gov with a copy to the Comptroller's open-records office: 'We run a public, non-commercial research benchmark that would archive daily copies of an aggregate query on Mixed Beverage Gross Receipts (naix-2893), monthly totals for one city, and publish those copies with their hashes so forecasts can be checked. Does the Texas Open Data Portal licence allow automated retrieval and public redistribution of these copies? Is there a licence that applies when a dataset's licence field is blank?'

target.population: Records in naix-2893 whose location_city, upper-cased, equals 'AUSTIN' and whose obligation_end_date_yyyymmdd is the target month's last day. This is the venue's city, not the taxpayer's mailing city (the doc's rule). Venues inside and outside city limits both count. inside_outside_city_limits_code_y_n is ignored, and location_city is the city label, not a boundary. All permit types and receipt categories are included. City spelling variants such as 'AUSTIN ' are covered by upper(), but variants like 'AUSTIN TX' are not [unverified; check in implementation]. Austin had 1,477 records for Sep 2026 [verified].
target.window: One calendar month, the reporting period that ends on obligation_end_date_yyyymmdd. The upload date is not the period.
target.calculation: Index = 100 x T(M) / T(M-12). T(M) is sum(total_receipts) for the population and month M in the resolution snapshot. T(M-12) is the same sum for the year-earlier month in the snapshot archived at lock. It is published and hashed with the question and is never re-read. Rows are summed as published. The published total_receipts is used, not the sum of components. A component check (liquor + wine + beer + cover = total) is logged, never used. An absent filing is absent, never a zero.
target.unit: Index points (100 = same nominal receipts as the same month last year)

lock: 23:59 America/Chicago on the last day of the month before the target month (the doc: 'before 00:00 America/Chicago on the first day of the target month'), stored in UTC. No publisher calendar exists, so the round text says that SSA sets and resolves the metric (docs/sources.md §1.1). At lock the newest usable month is M-2. On 2026-11-09 Sep 2026 was in and Oct 2026 held 5% of Austin's usual record count. Every round before the first scored one runs unscored, as the doc requires ('Until that threshold and resolution lag are validated, run unscored trials only'). Pilot: daily snapshots from the day the adapter reaches main. Cycle 1 is Oct 2026 (resolution snapshot Mon 2026-11-30). Cycle 2 is Nov 2026 (resolution Thu 2026-12-31). Each cycle's total is re-read in the three Saturday loads after its resolution. Verdict Fri 2027-01-22. First scored lock: Sun 2027-01-31 23:59 CT, provided written permission or the maintainers' clearance of the rights verdict has arrived by then (the arena connects no source without it; until then the pilot archives privately), for February 2027, resolving Wed 2027-03-31 12:00 CT. Working back: cycle 1 needs a Nov 30 snapshot, so the adapter must be on main with the refresh running by Sat 2026-11-28. That leaves about 20 days for owner approval, the PR to dev, review, and the separate dev-to-main merge (lesson 7). Participants get 9 weeks before the first scored lock. If main is reached later, cycle 1 becomes Dec 2026 (resolving Sun 2027-01-31), the verdict moves to about 2027-02-19, and the first scored lock moves to Sun 2027-02-28 for March 2027, the SXSW month.
baseline: Ranked zero point (owner decision, rev 2): same-as-last-year, index 100 (this month equals the same month last year). The doc lists it first ('Use a seasonal naive baseline and persistence in year-over-year growth'). Rev 2 writes it as one parameterised reference family rather than a new name: yoy(k=0, calendar=false, spread=rms12). Here k is the number of latest eligible months used for a growth adjustment, and k=0 means none. The Chicago card uses the same family with k=3, calendar=true. The round's zero_point holds these parameters, following the yoy4 pattern on track/seattle-community-calls-v2. Spread: sd = root-mean-square of (index - 100) over the 12 most recent target months that are complete in the lock capture (M-13 to M-2), all read from that one capture. Shown, not ranked: (a) the doc's growth reference, 100 x sum(T(M-2..M-4)) / sum(T(M-14..M-16)), from the lock capture. M-1 is not posted at lock, so 'latest three eligible months' means M-2 to M-4. (b) Persistence of growth, the index of M-2. Each gets its own 12-month RMS spread. Measured on 39 target months, 2023-07 to 2026-09 (modern backfill, not first prints). MAE in index points: seasonal naive 3.51 (median 2.21, max 15.96); doc growth reference 4.17 (median 2.97, max 13.62); persistence 4.83. Mean CRPS with the spreads above: seasonal naive 3.00, growth reference 3.31, persistence 3.78. The doc's reference scores -10.3% skill against seasonal naive. Houston (-12.8%), San Antonio (-6.3%) and Dallas (-2.1%) agree. Statewide, the growth reference is 4.5% better [verified computation]. Shock months, seasonal naive error then growth-reference error: Jul 2024 (Hurricane Beryl month) +10.1 / +9.8; Nov 2024 -7.7 / -13.6; Jun 2026 (FIFA World Cup month in Texas) -7.3 / -8.7; Jul 2026 -6.3 / -7.9; Sep 2026 -16.0 / -11.0. The Sep 2026 jump (+16% in Austin, +12% statewide) is unexplained, and it is a first print [unverified cause].
resolution: The first successful snapshot at or after 12:00 America/Chicago on the last calendar day of the month after the target month (the doc's rule). Example: February 2027 resolves on the Wed 2027-03-31 snapshot. Measured fill, as the share of today's total present by that date: Sep 2025 to Mar 2026, 83 to 89%; Apr to Aug 2026, 91 to 94%; Sep 2026, 99%. Waiting to the 10th of the month after adds only 0.5 to 4 points [verified computation from :created_at]. These numbers are lower bounds. Rows for every past month are deleted and re-inserted every week (for example 3,114 Sep 2025 to Aug 2026 rows were re-created in the 2026-10-31 and 11-07 loads, 1,026 of them for venues whose responsibility end date had just been set). Re-created rows look 'late' to :created_at even when they were there at first print. Only snapshots show the real first-print gap. The pilot measures it. Go if each cycle's Austin total moved by less than 1.0 index point (1%) across the three Saturday loads after its resolution snapshot, and if first-print Austin record counts are at least 97% of the year-earlier month's. No-go: rounds stay unscored, and a new revision moves the resolution later. Later revisions never change a resolved round.
missing_data_policy: (1) No successful snapshot within 24 hours of the resolution time: the round is void, never resolved from a later pull (the doc: 'void the question if no valid snapshot is obtained'). (2) Coverage check on the resolution snapshot: Austin's target-month record count must be at least 97% of T(M-12)'s record count in the lock capture. History never went below 100.7% over 2023-07 to 2026-09 [verified computation]. Otherwise the next daily snapshot inside the grace window is used, and if it still fails the round is void. (3) At lock: if any month the reference or its spread needs is missing, or under 90% of its year-earlier record count, the round is not posted. (4) A failed daily fetch is recorded and never back-filled. (5) Backtests use today's backfill and are labelled that way.
scoring: SSA topline scoring of a predictive distribution over the index: mean and sd, or quantiles including 0.5, scored with CRPS (continuous_normal). Skill = 1 - CRPS(entrant) / CRPS(yoy(k=0, spread=rms12)). Check that submitting the reference scores about 0, over the same 39 months: an entrant who submits index 100 and only rescales the sd gains at most +4.4%, at a scale of 0.55. The 12-month RMS runs wide (90% coverage 32/39, sd 1.9 to 16.7), because the 2023 covid-recovery months inflate the early sds. Calendar effect: each extra Friday plus Saturday in the target month, against last year, moves the index by about +1.5 points in Austin (correlation 0.21) and +2.5 in Houston (0.43), in-sample over 2023 to 2026. An entrant who counts weekends earns this without simulating anyone [verified computation]. Movement check (arena scoring.noise_floor on the last 36 monthly indices): Austin m = 4.45, s = 2.18; statewide m = 4.45, s = 0.00. Month-to-month movement in the index is mostly noise, so there is little room for skill on the regular tier. The doc's event tier and city profile are where skill can show.

The doc proposes Austin YoY, lock before the month, resolution at 12:00 CT on the last day of the next month, a seasonal naive plus a three-month growth baseline, unscored trials until the lag is validated, and an app token. It says 3,870,359 rows and a metadata update on Oct 31, 2026 08:32:43 UTC (checked Nov 6). That was the previous Saturday load. The next one landed 2026-11-07.

assumptions: Rev 2, owner decisions (Claude, delegated by Haoyang Shang, 2026-11-08). Rights: 'permission-needed', with the question to the portal drafted. This replaces rev 1's recommendation to score from a private archive meanwhile. Zero point: same-as-last-year with a 12-month RMS spread, as rev 1 recommended. Rev 1's runners-up stay on the board unranked: the doc's three-month growth reference, persistence, and a weekend-adjusted version (not built). Pilot: October and November 2026 as unscored rounds, verdict Fri 2027-01-22. The reference is renamed to the parameterised yoy(k=0, spread=rms12), from rev 1's 'snaive12' (G1).

Question picked from the doc's four: Austin YoY number, the regular tier. Reason: one number first (skill step 1), and it is the doc's first question. Runner-up: a five-city YoY profile (Austin, Houston, Dallas, San Antonio, Fort Worth) scored with the energy score. Its components move together (World Cup months +7% in Houston and Dallas), which is closer to what the track wants, and all five cities are measured in the evidence. The neighbourhood share and ranking questions need geocoding and a frozen boundary file, so they are left to a later card.

Lesson 14 tests as written. Behavioral: pass (spending at licensed venues adds up many people's choices; nominal dollars, so prices are in it too). Spatial: pass (venue city). Recurring: pass (weekly loads, monthly periods; no published posting calendar, so SSA sets the metric). Public and archivable: free and keyless pass; archive terms unclear (rights: permission-needed, rev 2). Prospective: pass (lock before the month is lived). Scorable: pass (one number from one snapshot).

The year-earlier month is read from the lock capture, which is a mature total, while the target is a first print. If first prints run low, the index carries a bias that every entrant faces and the pilot measures. Runner-up: reconstruct last year's first print from :created_at. That was rejected because the weekly re-inserts reset :created_at.

City filter upper(location_city) = 'AUSTIN', not a ZIP list or the inside-city-limits flag. Reason: it is the field the doc names, and it is stable as text. Runner-up: Austin ZIP codes, which would need a frozen list.
No app token, even though the doc suggests one: getting one means creating an account. Five grouped requests ran keyless in 0.5 to 5.4 s, and one a day is enough.

Daily fetch at 14:00 UTC, with an 800-day query window. Reason: 16 months for the reference, 12 past target months plus their year-earlier months for the spread (M-25), plus margin. Runner-up: a weekly Sunday fetch, which would miss the Wednesday holiday loads.

Suggested arena names: tracker 'tx_comptroller'; series 'austin_mixbev_yoy'; adapter ssa/adapters/tx_mixbev.py with a fetch_text/parse split; archive sources/tx_mixbev/<YYYY-MM-DD>.json; round_id 'austin-mixbev-<YYYY-MM>'; zero_point yoy(k=0, spread=rms12).
